policy: Wave B candidates require a bounded trigger and non-overlapping ownership before implementation.
A clear idea without a real repository problem case is insufficient for ADOPT.
Problem evidence may justify incubation but is not skill-effectiveness evidence.
DEFER means absent from REGISTRY.json and skills/ until a later real case justifies reconsideration.
MODIFY means the original candidate scope/name is too broad and must be narrowed before implementation.
Any created Wave B skill must start incubating, UNPROVEN, evidence_tier none.

problem_evidence: Phases 01-14 contain no bounded repository case centered on logs/metrics/traces or production incident diagnosis.
Existing testing and CI skills already own test/CI failure diagnosis; a new generic observability skill would currently be mostly speculative.

potential_ownership: correlating logs, metrics, traces, and runtime symptoms
overlap_risk: generic debugging workflows not owned by this repository

reconsider_when: a real runtime incident requires multi-signal diagnosis
the repository has a concrete service observability stack or incident artifact to evaluate
decisions.next_action: Do not create a skill in Chat 15B.

problem_evidence: The current repository has package/workspace guidance and compatibility/testing machinery, but no bounded dependency-upgrade migration case with recorded breakage/recovery evidence.
Creating a generic upgrade skill now would substantially overlap monorepo-typescript, testing-typescript-systems, api-contract-testing, and future runtime compatibility guidance.
reconsider_when: a real major-version dependency migration produces a bounded compatibility case
upgrade work requires reusable sequencing beyond package-manager/test guidance
decisions.next_action: Do not create a skill in Chat 15B.

problem_evidence: Phase 12 re-audit required an explicit distinction between format compatibility, architecture compatibility, tested host execution, and runtime loading.
PR #27 and its compatibility overclaim fixtures showed that support claims can drift even when repository tooling remains green.
api-contract-testing owns API/provider-consumer compatibility, leaving host/runtime/toolchain compatibility as a separate bounded concern.
decisions.rename_reason: The original compatibility-engineering scope is too broad and would overlap API contracts, dependency upgrades, database migrations, and release engineering. runtime-compatibility-engineering narrows ownership to host/runtime/toolchain/format compatibility claims and their evidence.

owns: cross-platform compatibility regressions and adaptation boundaries

overlap_review.api-contract-testing: API contract compatibility remains owned by api-contract-testing; this target owns host/runtime/toolchain compatibility.
overlap_review.ci-pipeline-reliability: CI may execute compatibility checks; this target defines the compatibility claim/evidence model rather than workflow signal integrity.
overlap_review.testing-typescript-systems: Testing supplies execution evidence; this target decides what environment/version support claim that evidence justifies.

minimum_criteria: distinguishes format/design compatibility from tested execution
does not infer macOS or arbitrary Linux support from Windows/Ubuntu evidence
records runtime/tool versions and environment scope
states adaptation-required boundaries for incompatible conventions

decisions.next_action: Keep incubating with explicit NOT_RUN behavioral evidence until a controlled post-creation compatibility case executes.

problem_evidence: Phase 10 proves installer rollback semantics, not production release promotion/rollback.
Phase 14 deliberately excluded production rollout/rollback from ci-pipeline-reliability, but no real release incident or deployment strategy has yet been evaluated in this repository.
Phase 17 release readiness is future work and should not be backfilled as evidence before execution.

overlap_risk: installer transaction logic for local skill installation

reconsider_when: Phase 17 or another real deployment/release produces a bounded rollout/rollback case
a production release failure/recovery exposes reusable decision rules
decisions.next_action: Do not create a skill in Chat 15B.

problem_evidence: Phase 13 established source/license provenance because external-source trust claims require explicit evidence.
Phase 11 CI executes third-party actions and Phase 14 ci-pipeline-reliability explicitly excludes supply-chain policy, leaving dependency/action/artifact trust without a specialist owner.
Installer/repository evidence already distinguishes checksums, provenance, and trusted source boundaries, but no skill currently owns software supply-chain integrity as a reusable concern.
decisions.rename_reason: The original supply-chain-security label is broad enough to include vendor governance and organizational policy. software-supply-chain-integrity narrows scope to technical trust of source dependencies, actions, build artifacts, provenance, and verification evidence.

owns: immutable or deliberately versioned third-party build inputs

overlap_review.application-security-local-first: Application security owns runtime/application trust boundaries; this target owns build/dependency/artifact provenance and integrity.
overlap_review.ci-pipeline-reliability: CI may enforce supply-chain gates, but this target defines what must be trusted/verified.
overlap_review.provenance-contract: Repository source attribution/licensing is evidence input; this target generalizes technical integrity rules without turning attribution into security proof.

minimum_criteria: separates version pinning from integrity/provenance evidence
requires an explicit verification mechanism for critical artifacts/dependencies
does not claim application security or release safety from supply-chain checks alone

decisions.next_action: Keep incubating with explicit NOT_RUN behavioral evidence until a controlled post-creation supply-chain case executes.

lock_claim: Wave B implementation is complete. Both created Wave B skills remain incubating and behaviorally UNPROVEN pending controlled post-creation execution; this lock is not an effectiveness promotion.
